Unmetered for NYT Privacy

What it stores

Your reading stays in your browser

The extension holds no code that could send it anywhere.

No account

No email, no password, no sign-in. The extension does not know who you are.

It calls nothing

No server, no device ID, no analytics, no remote fonts or scripts.

One stored value

It keeps one value on your computer: whether the switch is on.

NYT

It stands down for subscribers

When it finds a New York Times session it stops blocking, so it leaves a subscription you pay for alone.

nytimes.com

The one site it can see. Every other tab is invisible to it.

cookies

Reads one cookie name to spot a Times session, then forgets it.

storage

Holds the on/off setting, and has room for nothing else.

Host access covers nytimes.com and no other site. Source published under the Mozilla Public License 2.0.
